correctness.rationale: For the largest used generator prime \(P\ge5\), no numerator \(r+1\) from a smaller prime generator can contain \(P\): it would force \(r=P-1\), an even integer greater than two. Nor can a prime factor of \(P+1\) exceed \(P\). Hence the largest nonzero valuation is exactly \(-a_P\), so peeling recovers the exponent and strictly lowers the largest possible prime. At support \(\{2,3\}\), solving \(x=-u+2v\), \(y=u-v\) gives the stated cone and unique exponents. Reversing the forced steps proves sufficiency. The finite verifier is consistent with the symbolic proof.
correctness.risk: No asymptotic enumeration of the semigroup by height is claimed.

It proves uniqueness of an existing representation but does not provide a recognition/reconstruction criterion. Resultary search returned the audited theorem as the only exact hit; the Dedekind-psi OEIS entries concern related values but not this repeated-generator rational semigroup.

source_inspections.title: Product of Some Polynomials and Arithmetic Functions
source_inspections.trigger: Defines the exact product family, proves uniqueness and poses the image problem.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves an explicit published recognition problem by a finite deterministic decoder, not merely by another uniqueness argument. The terminal cone and exact integer corollary give a concise structural description that a future study of this semigroup can directly reuse.

final_claim: A positive rational belongs to the multiplicative semigroup generated by \((p+1)/p\) exactly when deterministic largest-prime peeling succeeds and the terminal \(2,3\)-valuation pair satisfies \(x+2y\ge0\) and \(x+y\ge0\); the representation is unique, and the representable positive integers are exactly the \(3\)-smooth integers.
limitations: Positive rationals and finitely supported nonnegative exponents only.
